disease_label_per_paper: Acute pericarditis following radiofrequency ablation of a metastatic liver tumor
presentation_summary: 56-year-old man with hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and metastatic liver tumor underwent radiofrequency ablation of a segment II liver lesion adjacent to the pericardium.
The next day he developed new-onset chest pain, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, fever, and chills.
Physical examination revealed a friction rub.
ECG showed diffuse ST elevation except in aVR and V1; baseline ECG had been normal.
WBC was 10,300/uL, CRP 19.8 mg/dL, CK 202 U/L, CK-MB 0.6 ng/mL, and troponin-I 0.013 ng/mL.
Echocardiography showed new small pericardial effusion about 1.12 cm without tamponade.
